text:
incident-bot: PAGER: outgoing-data-detect - High severity. Unusual large PUTs to external s3://redwood-logs-ext from log-relay-prod. Sample snippets reportedly include header fragments. Paging @marty_oncall.

marty_oncall: I'm on it, grabbing runbook https://go.runbook/log-relay-egress and heading to the bridge.

alice_ops: confirming - I'm tailing log-relay-prod. Seeing repeated PUTs to external bucket since ~02:14 UTC. Config rollout for configmap 'log-relay-bucket' at ~02:10 looks suspicious.

bob_sre: taking immediate network action: blocked egress to s3://redwood-logs-ext via fw rule rule-egress-430 and scaled log-relay deployment to 0 (k8s).

alice_ops: thanks. celine_security - sample from bucket includes lines like 'Authorization: Bearer eyJ...' Can we assume tokens leaked?

celine_security: Affirmative. Samples contain Authorization header fragments. Treat as potential leak of access tokens and any API keys present in headers. Immediate recommended actions:
- rotate the log-relay service account keys and any API keys used for uploads
- disable the S3 integration (make writes fail)
- snapshot the external bucket for forensics and set it to read-only
- gather list of files and sample contents for classification (PII?)

bob_sre: I can rotate the relay service account key now. Plan: create new key, update k8s secret, restart pods. Will need ops approval to disable the integration immediately.

dave_prod: potential customer impact: customer-a (enterprise), customer-b (small prod cluster), several internal test tenants. Recommend contacting enterprise accounts first.

emma_legal: Legal note: collect list of affected customers and check for PII before any external notice. If tokens/PII are confirmed in a public bucket we have 72h reporting obligations in some jurisdictions. Preserve chain of custody for all artifacts.

alice_ops: action items summary for immediate owners: 
- @bob_sre rotate relay SA key and rotate OAuth client secret if used
- @marty_oncall block egress (done) and coordinate support/customer messaging
- @celine_security snapshot bucket and run quick grep for headers/PII
- @emma_legal collect affected customer list + sign off on notice

bob_sre: running quick scan now. Command I'm using: ```aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-logs-ext --query 'Contents[?Size>`1000`].Key' | jq '.'```
Preliminary results: logs/2026-03-17/relay-02.log (contains header lines), logs/2026-03-17/relay-03.log, relay-04.gz.

celine_security: I see three files with header leaks. Starting immutable snapshot to our forensics bucket and restricting ACLs on redwood-logs-ext. Also requesting IDP team to revoke the OAuth client secret used by the relay and to rotate any session tokens issued after 02:00 UTC.

marty_oncall: I'm taking incident ownership for the next handoff window (until 03:00 UTC). I'll coordinate triage updates and timeline. Notifying trust + support to prep messaging drafts.

alice_ops: @emma_legal @celine_security confirm scope: do we rotate all customer-facing tokens broadly or target only relay keys and the OAuth client secret?

celine_security: Start targeted: rotate the relay SA keys and OAuth client secret immediately. If forensics shows user tokens or customer secrets present, escalate to broader revocation. For now, identify leaked tokens and revoke them individually.

bob_sre: rotation done for relay SA. New secret pushed: secret/log-relay-s3 (k8s). Pods restarted, egress block still active, old key disabled. Changelog: /ops/infra#123.

dave_prod: Support, draft: short notice to customer-a/customer-b stating incident, what was exposed (headers in logs), mitigations (keys rotated, integration disabled), and recommended customer actions (rotate any credentials they suspect). Hold for legal sign-off.

emma_legal: I'll review drafts. Also ensure we gather evidence of whether tokens were accessed (bucket access logs, CDN fetch logs). Don't send external notices until I sign off.

alice_ops: forensics ETA ~90m for full scan. Celine, please include token introspection results (revoked vs active) and whether any tokens show usage from unknown IPs.

celine_security: Will include. Initial assessment: no confirmed reads by third parties in our cloud access logs beyond public access to the external bucket; unknown if someone fetched files from the public location. Forensics team checking CloudFront and external access.

marty_oncall: Good work. Summary: block egress (done), rotate creds (done), snapshot bucket (in progress), legal review (pending), customer outreach (prep). I'll open an incident postmortem ticket and schedule follow-ups. Please add any new findings here. :thumbsup:
